newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: FOCUS-Despite Dow rise, Manila bourse not out of woods.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Despite Dow rise, Manila bourse not out of woods.

text.p: Philippine shares struggled for the third day running on Thursday despite gains by the Dow and brokers said they saw no major developments in the days ahead to lift the market out of its lethargy.
Analysts said the scheduled listing of Equitable Banking Corp on Thursday might release some cash into the market but doubted it could substantially push the main index up.
The market's main barometer slipped by 9.58 points, or 0.30 percent, closing at 3,162.21 points as losers outnumbered gainers 57 to 49.
All sub-indices, except for the oils, fell with the property sector posting the biggest loss on rumours -- officially denied -- that Empire East Land Inc was encountering financial difficulties.
Empire East, the housing development subsidiary of Megaworld Properies and Holdings Inc, closed 1.20 peso lower, or 12.37 percent, at 8.50 pesos. It was the third most actively traded issue.
"All these rumours concerning our cash position, all of these are not true. Our company is very strong," said Giovanni Ng, investor relations officer of Megaworld and Empire East.
Empire East president Gerardo Garcia said he expected 33 percent growth in revenues and profits up to the year 2000.
Manila shares, weighed down by a mixture of factors, drifted in a narrow band for most of the session despite Dow Jones' 27.57-point rise on Tuesday to close at 6,611.05 points.
"I think they take the cue when Dow drops but not when it rises," Cilette Liboro, research head of Citisecurities Inc said.
Liboro said fears of future hikes in U.S. interest rates and the controversy over the Busang gold find in Indonesia, which sparked selling of mining issues, continued to depress the market.
Analyst Russel Ong of Anscor-Hagedorn Securities said Equitable could release some liquidity into the market "but I don't think its pull would be that heavy."
Ong said many factors were bringing the market down.
"We're looking at the banking sector which is weak ... we're looking at the weakness of the property sector, so it's really several factors. But they'll run their course," he added.

Analysts said they did not expect the March inflation figure, which newspapers predicted might hover around 4.4 percent and is expected to be released either on Friday or Monday, to have any dramatic impact.
Stable food prices and lower fuel prices are expected to keep year-on-year Philippine inflation in March about steady at 4.6 percent compared with 4.4 percent in February, a Reuters poll showed.

The average figure taken from a forecast by six banks and securities firms this week is far below the 11.8 percent registered in March last year when the country experienced a severe shortage of rice.
